26938.description:
URGENT HIRING!
Bismark Maritime Limited is urgently looking for qualified individual to fill below position.
Vehicle Yard Receivable Clerk
Location: Lae, Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea
Job Summary:
Vehicle Yard Receivable Clerk plays important role in Shipping and Customer Service Department by ensuring the efficiency of vehicle cargo shipments in accordance with company standard operating procedure.   This position requires regular coordination with customers.
Key Responsibilities:
Coordinate with Motor Dealers on the delivery of motor vehicles and other types of units or machines as well as serving walk-in customers on all vehicle and RORO cargos.
Carry out vehicle inspections and complete corresponding documentations.
Ensure vehicles/ machines are properly arranged to its respective ports.
Coordinate with Operations, Warehouse and Shipping Documentations in ensuring the accuracy and timely shipment of vehicle/machine cargos.
Carry out related duties as role requires.

Education: minimum Grade 12.
At least 3-4 years within this field or related roles/position.
Holds valid Class 6 Driver’s License.
Capable in coordinating with Motor Dealers and walk-in customers on the delivery of Motor Vehicles, Trucks, Buses, Machines, Break Bulk Cargo including Roll On Roll Off cargo.
Solid knowledge in carrying out vehicle inspections and completing necessary documentations.
Keen to details and well organized.
Good mathematical and computer skills.
Able to foster sustainable relationships of trust through an open and interactive communication with customers and co-workers.
Possess a strong commitment to personal and job safety.
Able to work overtime and on weekends.
Sober habits, good work ethics, friendly, optimistic and strong team player.
Can easily adopt organization’s system and flow of work orders.
With proof of education credentials.
Must be residing within Lae or nearby.

The HR Manager
Bismark Maritime Limited

clearly mention the position applied in the subject line

26748.description:
Primary strategic and financial advisor to Retail and Cards leadership teams
Drive financial analysis, budgeting, and forecasting for a leading regional bank
Collaborate with senior leadership to shape strategy and decision-making
The Company
Our client is a leading financial services organisation operating across the Asia-Pacific region. The organisation is focused on innovation, data modernisation, and delivering customer-centric solutions. It is committed to exceptional service for its customers and communities while fostering an environment where employees can grow and progress.
The Role
The Finance Partner acts as a critical link between the Finance function and the business units, supporting financial management, governance, and commercial decision-making. Embedded within the business, you will work closely with the GM of Retail and the Head of Cards to provide the insights and forward-looking analysis necessary to enable informed strategic decisions.
Key Responsibilities
Serve as a financial co-pilot to business unit leadership, providing strategic advice that aligns with enterprise objectives.
Own and complete the budgeting and planning processes for the Retail and Cards business units.
Prepare and deliver accurate management reports, forecasts, and variance analysis to identify financial risks and opportunities.
Maintain strict compliance with BPNG prudential standards, risk management policies, and internal controls.
Develop and leverage strong internal networks across Finance and the wider bank to facilitate effective communication.
Collaborate with the wider FP&A team to improve reporting quality and leverage automation tools for increased efficiency.
Qualifications, Skills & Experience
Tertiary qualifications (bachelor's or higher) in Business, Accounting, or Economics are essential.
Professional certification with CPA PNG or an equivalent international body is required.
At least 3–5 years of management or financial accounting experience in financial services, or 6 years of senior accounting experience in another industry.
Strong proficiency in Excel, financial modelling, and scenario analysis. Prior experience with ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle) is essential.
An understanding of the Cards and Payments industry and exposure to banking industry challenges is highly desirable.
Advanced ability to present complex financial information in a compelling way and build consensus across diverse teams.
To apply for this position, interested candidates are asked to submit:
A cover letter addressing key criteria of the role
An updated CV in Microsoft Word format, outlining employment history, educational qualifications, and listing three referees (referees will only be contacted if shortlisted)
Our client's priority is to provide opportunities to high performing Papua New Guineans for this position.  Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Be part of a high-performing strategy and transformation team
Work closely with senior leadership on enterprise-wide initiatives
Join structured environment focused on performance, delivery and impact
About the Company
A well-established PNG-based company with diverse portfolio spanning property development, logistics, retail, and hospitality. The organisation has a long-standing presence in the market and continues to expand its operations across the country. It offers a professional and collaborative environment where employees are supported to grow and contribute to impactful projects.
About the Role
An opportunity exists for a detail-oriented and analytical Project Analyst to support a central strategy and transformation function. This role plays a key part in supporting project coordination, tracking execution, and maintaining structured reporting across strategic initiatives.
The role is suited to someone who is highly organised, comfortable working with data and reporting, and able to support senior stakeholders by ensuring projects remain on track, well-documented, and aligned to business priorities.

Conduct structured strategic, financial and operational analysis to support leadership decision -making

Work closely with internal stakeholders to ensure visibility and accountability across projects

Head of Technology & Investment Finance

finance function of a large Technology & Investment division in a complex enterprise environment

26676.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our Commercial team, you will assist with the co-ordination of all K92 Mining inventory aspects relating to materials. To ensure optimum cost effectiveness and timely provision of supplies. To minimize the impact of the department on the environment and ensure the workplace health & safety of employees, contractors and other stakeholders are maintained.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position mean you will
Ensure that all aspects of Category Management process are undertaken in accordance with established policy and procedures
Assist in weekly and monthly reports are run and acted upon to guarantee no stock outs in materials
Ensure the timely completion of all tasks for both staff and contractors
Ensure all daily stock takes are carried out in a timely manner and posted within 24 hours of stock count
Update Pronto with correct and accurate information in relation to cataloguing requirements.
Complete all Material data master additions and changes.
Assist in investigation of inventory discrepancies and obsolesces including relevant investigations.
Complete all ANSI requests within a timely fashion.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have the following
Minimum 2 years’ experience in industry with relevant experience
Experience with Pronto function to Support Inventory requirements.
Experience with storage and handling of Dangerous goods
Behaviour consistent with K92 Mining core values
Excellent problem solving and decision-making capability
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Experience communicating with vendors in PNG and internationally
Ability to communicate clearly with people at all levels of the organisation and engage all relevant stakeholders
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

We are currently seeking an experienced and driven Purchasing Administration Officer. This is a FIFO position and is based in Kutubu, SHP, and reports to the Facility Maintenance Coordinator.
Purchasing Administration Officer
Job Summary
The Purchasing Administration Officer is responsible for coordinating end-to-end procurement activities to support maintenance operations. The role manages supplier relationships, purchasing through client systems, and inventory control, while providing day-to-day administrative support.
Key Responsibility Areas
Coordinate end-to-end procurement for maintenance activities, including supplier sourcing, quotation requests, and contract negotiations.
Process purchase requisitions and purchase orders through client procurement systems.
Monitor, control, and maintain inventory levels for maintenance supplies, tools, and equipment.

Proficient in procurement/ERP systems (including SAP) and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make sound decisions under pressure.
Excellent organisational and time-management skills, with strong attention to detail.

27007.description:
Porgera | Project Estimator - Engineering Projects [228363]
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
NPL now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual as
Project Estimator - Engineering Projects.
About the role
Reporting to the Superintendent Engineering Projects, the Project Estimator will play a critical role in ensuring cost accuracy across the full capital project lifecycle—from early-stage gate submissions through to final Approval for Expenditures (AFE). The
Project Estimator  - Engineering Projects
will provide detailed cost estimates, review project changes, and ensure robust financial inputs into the organisation’s capital portfolio.
In this role, you will
:
Develop and maintain an estimating tool based on schedule of rates
Conduct detailed reviews of engineering deliverables, scopes of work, project schedules, and execution plans
Prepare accurate material take-offs (MTOs), cost plans, and estimates for stage gate submissions and AFEs
Produce detailed cost reports, analysis, and supporting documentation for stakeholders
Work closely with Supply & Purchasing teams on Request for Quotations and streamlined procurement processes
Support the establishment and maintenance of preferred vendor lists
Review all capital project costs and ensure lifecycle cost contingencies are incorporated
Coordinate and consolidate estimation inputs across business units
Mentor and guide project personnel on estimating best practices
Review project changes, variations, and tender bids, providing recommendations
Assist project managers in assembling preliminary budgets for capital portfolio submissions
About You
You are a detail driven and analytical professional with deep experience in project cost estimation within major resource, infrastructure, or industrial sectors.
To be successful, you will have:
Minimum 10 years’ experience as a project cost estimator within mining, oil & gas, or major infrastructure (PNG or Australia highly regarded)
Qualifications in Quantity Surveying, Engineering, Project Management, or an extensive trades background
Strong ability to interpret technical documents, scopes of work, engineering drawings, and project schedules
A methodical approach to developing material take-offs and cost estimates
Experience with project life cycles and lifecycle costing methodologies
Demonstrated experience working collaboratively across multiple departments
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders on estimation accuracy and risk
Previous PNG estimation experience (highly regarded)
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a Project Estimator - Engineering Projects
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a
Project Estimator - Engineering Projects
. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.
Note
: This advert will be open until
11
th
May 2026
.  If you do not hear from NPL within two (2) weeks of this date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity
.

26964.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
To support the Mine Geothermal Team and other professionals to provide geothermal risk management and geothermal technical support to the Mine Technical and Operations teams.
Essential Duties
Drives and influence proactive safety behaviours within workgroups through visible leadership.
Ensures all personnel, visitors and contractors comply with site and contractual HSE requirements and hold people accountable for adherence.
Plans work so that it can be conducted safely; and considers environmental conditions, nearby activities, and the people and other resources needed to complete the work
Creates opportunities for people to work together to enable them to contribute to the business and learn from each other.
Provides training of mine technical and operational personnel in geothermal hazards and controls
Identify and manage geothermal hazards and associated risks successfully in the open pit by capturing and analysing geotechnical drilling, mapping and temperature data and through field regular inspections
Develops and communicates mine geothermal risk reviews for monthly and weekly mine plans
Delivers work within approved budget managing any variances in accordance with escalation process.
Actively seeks cost reduction opportunities.
Training & Experience
Tertiary qualified Bachelor of Science (Geology) or Engineering (Geotechnical, Reservoir) is essential and accreditation from the Institute of Engineers PNG Inc. and will be completed as part of work permit process. PNG Drivers License essential.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Embodies Newmont’s vision and values leading by example.
Develops & implements mid to short-term departmental plans, changes and initiatives to achieve overall business goals by providing positive leadership, direction & guidance within the department and wider organisation.
3+ years relevant work experience in a mining environment in a geotechnical/geothermal position is desirable.
Exposure in geothermal, geotechnical/geothermal monitoring systems is desirable.
Proficient in English with excellent verbal, written communication and public speaking skills.
Computer proficiency in MS Office suite.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Competent with modelling software such as Minesight, Leapfrog is preferable.
About Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

26913.description:
Auto Electrician
(The experienced, no-shortcuts kind)
Location: PNG Motors Port Moresby
Important:
If you do not have proven auto electrical experience, please do not submit your CV.
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading automotive groups, representing brands like Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Our workshops run on accuracy, discipline, and technical skill — and auto electrical work is where guesswork gets expensive.
We’re looking for an experienced
Auto Electrician
to join our Port Moresby workshop and take on the electrical work others usually get called in to fix.
This is not a role for someone learning on the job. If your experience is limited, this is not the one to test it on.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for diagnosing, repairing, and installing vehicle electrical systems across multiple brands. That includes fault finding, reading wiring diagrams, tracing electrical issues, and carrying out clean, reliable repairs that hold up in real conditions.
You’ll work on everything from starting and charging systems to sensors, ECUs, lighting, accessories, and electronic faults. You’ll also handle fit-outs and installations including radios, alarms, GPS units, and other electrical accessories.
The expectation is simple: diagnose properly, wire it properly, fix it properly.
Who This Suits
This role suits a qualified Auto Electrician with real workshop experience and the confidence to work without being carried.
You know how to fault-find properly, not guess. You understand modern vehicle systems, can read wiring diagrams, and know the difference between a clean install and a future comeback.
You work well with technicians, service advisors, and parts teams. You keep your work tidy, your job cards accurate, and your standards high.
If people already call you when the hard electrical jobs land, this will feel familiar.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
PNG Motors operates busy workshops with real volume, real standards, and real expectations. You’ll be working with recognised global brands, proper tools, and experienced teams who understand the value of good technical people.
This is a workshop where skill is noticed, standards matter, and good tradesmen are taken seriously.
How to Apply
If you’re reading this and thinking, “This is exactly where I should be,” then we want to hear from you.
Send your CV and cover letter to
[email protected]

26962.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Electrical Engineer is responsible for providing minor electrical design and modifications within the process plant and associated mine site infrastructure that shall meet company specifications, comply with operational requirements, agreements and relevant standards.
Essential Duties
Efficiently manage minor to medium projects to ensure they are completed as per agreed schedule, on budget and as per quality standards.
Review and investigate proposed electrical design within the plant and other mine site infrastructure and provide engineering guidance.
Complete engineering scope of works, develop design concepts, complete design and review drawings to ensure compliance with design scope and relevant standards.
Conduct load and cable calculations to ensure design is suitable for application.
Ensure all engineering activities meet the company’s business needs and consistently maintain high standards of occupational health, safety and environment.
Inspect completed installations and observe operations to ensure conformance to design and equipment specification and compliance with operational safety standards.
Effectively communicate day-to-day issues with the engineering teams and other work groups to develop good working relationships and report regularly on projects progress.
Recommend solutions to address issues that arise during construction work.
Training & Experience
Bachelor’s Degree qualification in Electrical Engineering
Registered with IEPNG
Valid Class 6 Driving License
3-5 years of electrical engineering experience in a mining industry environment.
Demonstrated competence in the application of Australian Standards in electrical design.
Strong technical capability in power systems and industrial instrumentation.
Experience in the use of PowerPac Software.
Strong capability to perform relevant engineering calculations to support designs.
Able to read, understand and prepare engineering drawings.
Capability to review engineering drawings and red-line in consultation with the design team to ensure accurate design and construction drawings.
Strong attention to detail and documentation capability.
Excellent communication skills and ability to work with minimal supervision.
Good computer literacy and understanding of Microsoft software suite.
Understanding of safety compliance and regulations.
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21/21 roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of
GEDSI Officer
to be based in
Port Moresby, National Capital District.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
In our continued effort to bring change WVPNG has entered into a partnership project with UN Women, local NGO Femili PNG and CSO Magna Carta to building on the gains of the EU-UN Spotlight Initiative to Eliminate Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) in PNG, UN Women, UNFPA and UNOPS (Agencies) have commenced implementation of a joint initiative entitled “Soim Wokabaut: Gender-Based Violence Referral Pathways Programme”, financed under the Neighborhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI Global Europe).
The purpose of this role is to provide technical guidance from gender and social inclusion perspectives into key project outcomes, and integrating planned GEDSI activities, particularly in the realms of gender, disability, and social inclusion. Furthermore, the role necessitates ensuring the project's adequate support through organizing COH Workshops with facilitators, supporting capacity building for local NGO, FBO & CSO Partners.

Ensure ongoing implementation on the Project
Ensure planned GEDSI activities with the project are executed in a timely manner.
Continue establishing and meeting partners as regularly planned. Representing Project in GEDSI stakeholders meeting and special event (20 days of Human Rights Activism)
Support GEDSI Coordinator coordinate implementation of gender technical program and provide field insight to support in accordance with WV PNG’s gender technical program to Area Program and Project
Monthly reporting and budget acquittals as scheduled

Collaborate with and support (local resource persons) other women-based groups to report and share learnings on main GEDSI indicators at the local context from a Do-No-Harm perspective.
Coordinate with GEDSI Coordinator to provide support and capacity building to World Vision staff and partners including other stakeholders on key project models such as the channels of hope for gender-models.

Know, understand and appreciation of World Vision’s Vision, Mission Statement and history to value your difference in deepen Our Promise to improving Wellbeing of all.

Comply and exercise organizational values and culture with CHIRPP
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Bachelor in Social Work, Psychology. Community Development or Gender Field/Background  or other relevant qualifications and experience including
Certificate of participation in safeguarding in other organizational or voluntary services

Experience social work or GEDSI related work, GEDSI integration. Networking skills with government bodies and donors, and experience with disability work and sector.

The MEAL Coordinator will oversee the systematic collection and analysis of objective, verifiable evidence to monitor the project's progress toward meeting its objectives and aligning with World Vision Papua New Guinea's strategic plan.

MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Program Design
Support the Program Impact and Effectiveness Manager in leading the development of the Education Portfolio Project proposals, with a focus on MEAL inputs, including the logframe, MEAL activity budget, and staffing, and the MEAL narrative plan.
Develop 3S and Education Portfolio-specific MEAL frameworks in coordination with project staff.
Support Program Impact and Effectiveness Manager as requested (WVPNG, strategy, sectoral frameworks, overall, MEAL system set-up, ad-hoc requests)
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting
Develop methodologies, sampling plans, and tools for outcome and process monitoring studies, including pre-/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, FGDs, and KIIs, for the 3S Project and Education Portfolio.

Conduct ITT verifications for the 3S Project each month in coordination with project staff, ensuring that project-level ITTs are updated with accurate data. Share key findings with management during the program review meetings.
Conduct regular project site visits and oversee partner and direct implementation to ensure quality standards through scheduled inspections, data audits, and spot checks.
Ensure that the project team and other stakeholders discuss and address critical MEAL findings and recommendations.

Sensitize community members to their rights to information, consultation, participation, and to provide feedback and complaints, while emphasizing their responsibility to support solutions.

Attend internal and external meetings relevant to assigned projects
Attend internal and external training sessions, workshops, and events.

POSITION DESCRIPTION
TITLE
Programs Coordinator - WaSH and Nature based solutions (nbs)
REPORTING TO
Senior Program Manger
LOCATION
Pomio, East New Britain Province
EMPLOYMENT BASIS
Three-years contract (subject to three months’ probation)
Overview
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on the National Capital District, and Central Province in the Southern Region and East Sepik Province.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to act. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission.
WaterAid is open to employing and working with People Living with any forms of impairment and disability and other marginalized population.
JOB DIMENSION
About the Project
The PacFresH2O (Protecting Freshwater Resources for Increased Climate Resilience in the Pacific Islands) project is a multi-year initiative running from February 2024 to January 2031, aimed at enhancing climate resilience in rural communities of Papua New Guinea (PNG) and the Solomon Islands (SLB). Funded through the International Climate Initiative (IKI) and led by GIZ in partnership with the Pacific Community (SPC) and various national government bodies, the project responds to pressing climate-related challenges like drought, flooding, and cyclones that threaten water resources and infrastructure. It seeks to address the low levels of access to safe drinking water—particularly in rural and marginalised communities through integrated water management and sustainable, community-based interventions.
The project’s core strategy is built around three outputs: strengthening governance, coordination, and data use; implementing phased, climate-resilient water and sanitation solutions; and embedding Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) priorities into national policy frameworks. A key focus is on showcasing underutilised resources such as groundwater, improving meteorological and hydrological capabilities, and training local and national actors, including women and marginalised groups in climate finance and evidence-based water resource management. Through these efforts, PacFresH2O aims to create scalable and replicable models for rural water resilience, boosting the adaptive capacity of Pacific Island nations in the face of climate change
Purpose of the Role
The Program Coordinator – WaSH and NBS will play a crucial role in ensuring the successful implementation of project activities, strengthening coordination, and supporting strategic alignment with consortium partners and stakeholders. Additionally, the Program Coordinator will have supervisory responsibilities, overseeing the work of Program Officer for Pomio District to ensure effective delivery of project components
The Program Coordinator will be responsible for facilitating multi-level coordination, overseeing project implementation, supervising staff, and ensuring compliance with donor and partner requirements. This includes working closely with WaterAid, GIZ, SPC, and government agencies to ensure effective planning, execution, and reporting of activities in Pomio District, while preparing for full-scale implementation upon project commissioning (expected late 2025).
Location
This position will be based in Pomio District, East New Britian Province.
Line Manager
Senior Program manager ENB
Budget
The role will support budget management for local operations.
Team Membership
WaterAid Rabaul, NCD and Central Programs team.
Documentation and Reporting
Inputs to quarterly reports and general weekly progress reports. Will also assist with documentation concerning monitoring, evaluation, knowledge and learning.
Key Performance Areas
Project Coordination & Implementation Oversight
Lead the implementation of preparation phase activities, ensuring alignment with project goals and timelines.
Manage target community selection, coordinating with the Pomio District Development Authority (DDA) and District WASH Committee (DWC) to reaffirm priorities based on Pomio District’s 5-year climate-resilient WASH plan and the National WaSH Policy (2015-2030).
Oversee WASH and Water Resource baseline, ensuring data-driven decision-making and targeted interventions within the target communities.
Lead data collection processes in target communities, including undertaking Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) Survey
Stakeholder Engagement & Multi-Level Coordination
Serve as the primary liaison between WaterAid, GIZ, SPC, and government partners in East New Britain to streamline project implementation.
Strengthen collaboration with the East New Britain Provincial Administration (ENBPA), District Development Authority and East New Britain Provincial Health Authority (ENBPHA) for policy alignment.
Ensure effective communication with Rabaul District Development Authority regarding project adjustments due to implementation focus on Pomio District.
Supervision & Team Leadership
Provide guidance and oversight to the Program Officer for Pomio District, ensuring efficient execution of their responsibilities.
Foster a collaborative and inclusive team environment, supporting professional growth and skill-building for staff.
Conduct regular check-ins, mentoring, and performance evaluations to maintain high-quality project delivery.
Policy Support & Institutional Strengthening
Support policy reviews and advocacy efforts, ensuring integration of climate adaptation and gender-responsive WASH governance into PNG’s national frameworks.
Work with GIZ and SPC to align local WASH interventions with PNG’s National Adaptation Plan (NAP), Medium-Term Development Plan IV (MTDP IV), and climate resilience strategies.
Ensure district and provincial WASH committees receive technical capacity building and structured support for improved governance.
Data Management & Knowledge Generation
Oversee the development of baseline data collection frameworks, ensuring inclusion of key informant interviews, focus group discussions, household surveys, and participatory rural appraisals
Lead Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) surveys to assess community freshwater resource management and climate change adaptation needs.
Work with consortium partners to analyse findings and integrate lessons into project adaptation strategies.
Compliance, Reporting, & Financial Oversight
Ensure compliance with donor requirements, working closely with WaterAid PNG’s finance and grant management team to uphold transparency and contractual obligations.
Lead project documentation and reporting, ensuring timely submission of updates to consortium partners.
Coordinate with WaterAid National Program Manager – WaSH system Strengthening, Australia’s Technical Lead – Planning and Monitoring and Program Coordinator in Melbourne to maintain strategic alignment and donor engagement.
The role requires engagement with a moderate degree of complexity, due to the need to:
Coordinate with multiple stakeholders, including formal program partners, as well as community leaders, traditional landowners and government agencies.
Ensure that risks concerning financial mismanagement and fraud are adequately managed.

High travel requirements within Pomio District. Occasional travel to Port Moresby. Possible travel to other districts in the East New Britain Province, as needed.
Level of contact with children
The role may involve baseline and supervision work in schools in East New Britian Province, as well as general work on WASH in Communities, Schools and Healthcare Facilities (HCFs). The position will be required to maintain WaterAid child safeguarding principles and standards at all times.

Essential

Experience in networking and liaising key stakeholders within government and civil

POSITION DESCRIPTION
TITLE
Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Coordinator
REPORTING TO
Senior Program Manager, East New Britain
LOCATION
Kokopo or Rabaul, East New Britain Province
START DATE
END DATE
June 2026
31 December 2028
Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is within the National Capital District, Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province in the Momase region and East New Britain Province in the New Guinea Islands. We work nationally through a system strengthening approach with the Government of PNG.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
Position Summary
WaterAid is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Coordinator to join our team in East New Britain Province. The role will work collaboratively with the project implementation team to coordinate collection, analysis, reporting and use of project monitoring from two key projects: The PacFresh H20 Program implemented in Rabaul and Pomio districts and the KIWA Initiative implemented in Rabaul district. The role will also involve close collaboration with WaterAid PNG Headquarters located in Port Moresby, and the Regional team based in Australia. They will also contribute to broader organisational learning initiatives, helping to share key lessons from East New Britain across the region.
About the Projects
The Protecting Freshwater Resources in the Pacific (PacFresh H2O) Project aims to strengthen the climate resilience of rural communities in Rabaul and Pomio districts by improving access to safe, reliable water and sanitation, protecting freshwater resources, and advancing gender equality and social inclusion. Through a system-strengthening approach, the project builds the skills of local decision-makers and community groups, improves coordination and planning, implements priority measures to address water insecurity, and supports the scale-up of climate-resilient WASH approaches through stronger policy integration, learning and financing. The project ensures that women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups benefit from more resilient WASH services and improved livelihoods.
The Kiwa Initiative Preserve Project aims to strengthens climate resilience in vulnerable rural and coastal communities by protecting and restoring freshwater and watershed ecosystems through nature-based solutions. The project seeks to improve reliable access to safe water, reduce climate-related risks such as droughts, flooding and contamination, and promote community-led resource management that embeds gender equality, disability inclusion and local knowledge. By building the capacity of government partners, community groups and rights-holder organisations, the project embeds sustainable ecosystem management practices and supports more resilient and secure livelihoods in the face of increasing climate impacts.
Key performance areas / Accountabilities
Project Monitoring
Work with Programs Team members to develop, implement and review project-level monitoring, evaluation and learning frameworks and theories of change to ensure they are feasible, meaningful, and fit for purpose.
Lead development of data collection tools and coordinate regular collection of quantitative and qualitative project monitoring data aligned with project MEL Frameworks.
Lead and oversee the MEL framework in WaterAid Programme Systems (WAPS) updating the indicator and results for the projects and report to the SMT and WA Regional Team.
Ensure all the indicators and results are updated and reviewed on monthly and quarterly basis and reported aligning to the CCPM.
Build capacity of project staff and partners in MEL and support regular analysis of data to inform project activities and reporting.
Ensure that cross cutting issues, such as gender equality, disability equity, climate change and sector strengthening are adequately and appropriately reflected in project MEL Frameworks and reporting.
Identify opportunities to further engage the community in the planning, monitoring and review of WASH services and work with local authorities and community representatives to design and implement feedback mechanisms about community access to water, sanitation and hygiene services.
Leader the use of dashboard in WAPS to monitor the programming work and the support to provide fortnightly and monthly.
Support the filling of the WA Risk template offline and upload to WAPS register and regular monitor and update in WAPS.
Project reviews and evaluation
Support project reviews and evaluations, including contributing to developing Terms of Reference, coordinating in-country field work, collating and sharing existing project monitoring data with the evaluation team and contributing to sense-making activities.
Support the program team to carry-out the Project Health Checks using the template in WAPS and review the MEL information and complete the rating for projects on six monthly bases.
Learning & Documentation
Support to gather information on practices in the field and support staff and partners to document best practices from their work and disseminate internally and externally
Collect and disseminate results, best practices and lessons learned internally and externally
Support the Senior Program Manager to organise and facilitate regular project reflections and contribute to broader organisational reflections such as quarterly reflection meetings and annual meetings.
Support WaterAid staff and partners to use WAPS M&E data and information to improve programme and organisational performance. Develop and coordinate learning processes between project teams within WaterAid PNG and implementing partners to encourage cross-project learning and information sharing.
Actively promote and engage in learning processes between WaterAid country programs and contribute to global publications and global learning events based on the PNG experience
Communications and Working Relationships
Internal
WaterAid PNG
WaterAid Australia (participation in learning events etc)
WaterAid global intranet (participation in webinars and other online learning platforms)
External
Multiple governmental, non-government and community stakeholders
Physical Environment and Demands
High travel requirements within East New Britain Province and potentially occasional travel to Port Moresby.
Level of contact with children
The role may involve engaging with communities to develop and collect monitoring information, and as such may come into contact with children. The position will be required to maintain WaterAid child safeguarding principles and standards at all times.
Person Specification and Selection Criteria
The following criteria will be used to assess candidates for the post.
All applicants must address these criteria in their application:
Criteria
Experience
--      Substantial experience working on monitoring, evaluation and learning in the community/ international development sector (experience in the WASH sector is an advantage but not essential), including designing monitoring tools, collecting data and analysing and reporting.
--      Experience integrating cross-cutting issues such as gender equality and social inclusion, climate change and sector strengthening into MEL systems.
Knowledge and skills
--      A thorough understanding of, and experience using different monitoring and evaluation theories and practices, including both qualitative and quantitative approaches.
--      A high degree of knowledge of theory of change and how to use data and evidence to improve practice.
--      An understanding of gender equality and social inclusion issues in the PNG context, and good practice approaches to addressing these.
--      Knowledge of good practice capacity building approaches and skills to implement them.
Education
--      Minimum Bachelor degree in a relevant field such as Project Management, Social Sciences, Development Studies or a related field.
Personal qualities
--      Commitment to WaterAid’s values and safeguarding standards
--      Personable with a sensitivity to the communication styles of external stakeholders and internal staff.
--      Confidence working with both government and non-government stakeholders.
--      Commitment to the ‘Do No Harm’ approach to aid and development work.
Recruitment process
This position is open to Papua New Guinean candidates only.
Applications for this role must comprise of:
An application letter addressing the essential person specification criteria outlined above (maximum 2 pages).
A curriculum vitae (maximum 4 pages). The CV must include three professional referees (referees will not be contacted until after interviews, with permission from the candidate).
Applications which do not address the Selection Criteria specified and the page limits will NOT be considered.

REPORTING TO

EMPLOYMENT BASIS:

Overview
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on Central Province in the Southern Region and East Sepik Province
Since 2018, WaterAid has been working with district and provincial government stakeholders including the East Sepik Provincial Health Authority (ESPHA) and Wewak District Development Authority (DDA) to implement a district-wide program that aims to support government-led WASH service delivery in Wewak District. The
Inclusive WASH for Wewak District
program, funded under the Australian Government’s (DFAT)
Water for Women Program
, will run for five years.The WaterAid office in Wewak town will take the lead on partner engagement and co-delivery of WASH projects. The Port Moresby office will provide strategic and technical support and lead on engagement with national government.
WaterAid works through supporting local organizations and government and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Our Mission and Vision
WaterAid’s mission is to transform the lives of the poorest and most marginalized people by improving access to WASH. Our vision is that all Papua New Guineans should have access to WASH by 2030.
Our Values
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
--       Respect
--       Accountability
--       Courage
--       Collaboration
--       Innovation
--       Integrity
WASH in PNG
In 2015 the government launched the country’s first National WASH Policy, which has led to the setting of clear WASH targets and priority areas for action. PNG has also signed off on a new WASH in Schools policy (as of April 2018), which will help to draw attention to the urgent need for improved WASH facilities in schools.
The implementation of the National WASH Policy is being led by the development of five year District WASH Plans to drive service delivery in the districts. Several donors are currently working with the WASH PMU to resource the development of District WASH Plans and facilitate learning on the process. District WASH Plans should be supported with annual budgets, to be funded through District Service Improvement Program (DSIP) funding and other government grants.
The drive for district level service delivery within the framework of the national WASH policies creates new opportunities to increase access to WASH services. PNG is now one of only three countries globally that has safe water coverage of less than 50% and has the twelfth highest proportion of people using unimproved sanitation. The positive changes in the enabling environment therefore need to lead to better planning for WASH services and an increase in public expenditure on WASH services.

Overview
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on the National Capital District, and Central Province in the Southern Region and East Sepik Province.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity

Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to act. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission.
WaterAid is open to employing and working with People Living with any forms of impairment and disability and other marginalized population.
JOB DIMENSION
About the Project
The PacFresH2O (Protecting Freshwater Resources for Increased Climate Resilience in the Pacific Islands) project is a multi-year initiative running from February 2024 to January 2031, aimed at enhancing climate resilience in rural communities of Papua New Guinea (PNG) and the Solomon Islands (SLB). Funded through the International Climate Initiative (IKI) and led by GIZ in partnership with the Pacific Community (SPC) and various national government bodies, the project responds to pressing climate-related challenges like drought, flooding, and cyclones that threaten water resources and infrastructure. It seeks to address the low levels of access to safe drinking water—particularly in rural and marginalised communities through integrated water management and sustainable, community-based interventions.
The project’s core strategy is built around three outputs: strengthening governance, coordination, and data use; implementing phased, climate-resilient water and sanitation solutions; and embedding Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) priorities into national policy frameworks. A key focus is on showcasing underutilised resources such as groundwater, improving meteorological and hydrological capabilities, and training local and national actors, including women and marginalised groups in climate finance and evidence-based water resource management. Through these efforts, PacFresH2O aims to create scalable and replicable models for rural water resilience, boosting the adaptive capacity of Pacific Island nations in the face of climate change
Purpose of the Role
The Program Officer will play a critical role in supporting the implementation of the PacFresh H2O Project. This role will focus on coordinating field activities, managing data collection processes, and ensuring effective engagement with community and government stakeholders. The Program Officer will work closely with the Program Coordinator and GEDSI Officer to ensure project activities align with established objectives and contribute to the long-term success of the initiative

This position is based in Pomio District, East New Britain Province

Assist in capacity-building efforts for local stakeholders, ensuring communities understand and actively participate in project activities.
Data Collection & Information Management
Work with the Program Coordinator and consortium partners to refine the data collection framework, ensuring alignment with project objectives.
Lead key informant interviews, focus group discussions, household surveys, and participatory rural appraisals to gather baseline WASH and WRM data.
Support water resource mapping, emphasizing resilience, adaptation measures, and the integration of GEDSI principles.
Ensure all collected data is properly documented and analysed for reporting and decision-making.
Knowledge Generation & Research Support
Support surveys focused on freshwater resource management and climate change adaptation.
Assist in compiling findings into survey reports, contributing insights that inform inclusive adaptation measures.
Provide technical support for policy review discussions, ensuring local implementation experiences help shape national frameworks.
Policy Alignment & Institutional Strengthening
Support coordination efforts between WaterAid, GIZ, SPC, and government agencies to ensure policy frameworks align with project implementation
Work with provincial and district authorities to ensure WASH activities contribute to climate resilience objectives within PNG’s National Adaptation Plan (NAP) and Medium-Term Development Plan IV (MTDP IV).
Ensure knowledge-sharing activities effectively engage stakeholders in meaningful policy discussions.

Assist in coordinating field visits, stakeholder meetings, and training sessions, ensuring smooth execution of project activities.
Work with the Program Coordinator to ensure that all financial reporting and documentation comply with donor requirements.

Must be able to travel to projects sites within Pomio District as well as provincial office when required.

The role may involve baseline and supervision work in Communities, Schools and Health Care Facilities in Pomio District. The position will be required to always maintain WaterAid child safeguarding principles and standards all times.
Person Specification and Selection Criteria
This role has been created to recruit recent graduates with a tertiary qualification in environmental health, Social Sciences or Development Studies. Prior work experience with WASH, health or community development is desirable.

The project is led by WaterAid Australia, the primary beneficiary and contracting entity with the French Development Agency (AFD) through the Kiwa initiative, a regional multi-donor fund (EU, France, NZ, Australia and Canada). Live & Learn Environmental Education will act as an implementing partner, focusing on activities in Papua New Guinea and Samoa. Permatil Global, another implementing partner, will lead efforts in Timor-Leste.

26885.description:
JOB ADVERTISEMENT
Be Part of a National Model for Community‑Led Conservation
This consultancy offers a rare opportunity to contribute to one of PNG’s most respected community‑based conservation initiatives. Your expertise will help strengthen governance systems that protect biodiversity, support local livelihoods, and shape national best practices for protected area management. If you’re passionate about conservation, governance, and community empowerment in Papua New Guinea, we’d love to hear from you.
Consultancy Opportunity: YUS Conservation Area Governance & Management Effectiveness
Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program – Papua New Guinea (TKCP‑PNG)
Contract Duration:
May 2026 – December 2027 (actual duration may change)
Location:
Lae, with travel to YUS Conservation Area in Kabwum, Morobe Province.
About YUS Conservation Area and Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program
The YUS Conservation Area is Papua New Guinea’s first Conservation Area, spanning 162,683 hectares from the Saruwaget Range to the Bismarck Sea. Most of the conservation area is located in YUS Local Level Government, Kabwum District, Morobe province. The conservation area was gazetted in 2009 under the Conservation Areas Act of 1978. The area provides protection for a broad range of endemic and endangered species, promotes sustainable management of natural resources by its 15,000 indigenous residents among 50 remote villages, and serves as a national model for the conservation of customary-owned land. The YUS Conservation Area is governed by Conservation Area Management Committee comprising of all levels of government representative and community representative through their community-based organisation.
Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program-PNG is a local NGO based in Lae, Morobe Province that provides technical support in the management of the YUS Conservation Area. Formally established in 2013, its technical staff implement programs across wildlife research and monitoring, community livelihoods and sustainability.
About the Opportunity
The Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program – PNG (TKCP‑PNG) is seeking a highly qualified
specialist organisation or individual consultant
to lead a major governance and community‑capacity strengthening initiative across the YUS Conservation Area.
This consultancy is part of TKCP’s multi‑year effort to strengthen community‑based governance, improve stakeholder accountability, and enhance management effectiveness for PNG’s first nationally designated Conservation Area. The work is supported by the British Government under the Darwin Initiative.
The successful consultant will work closely with TKCP’s Governance & Engagement Manager to deliver targeted training, coaching, participatory assessments, and practical tools that empower Ward Councillors, Community‑Based Organisations (CBOs), and community leaders to fulfil their roles in conservation governance.
Why This Work Matters
The YUS Conservation Area spans 163,000 hectares and protects globally significant biodiversity, including the endangered Matschie’s tree kangaroo. It is home to more than 15,000 people across 50 villages, all of whom rely on customary land and local governance systems.
Recent assessments (METT 2021, SAPA 2021) highlight critical gaps in governance, representation, and coordination between communities and government stakeholders. Strengthening these systems is essential to ensuring long‑term conservation success and improved community well‑being.
This consultancy will directly contribute to:
Improved community participation in protected area governance
Stronger Ward‑level planning and representation
Increased capacity of newly formed CBOs
More effective stakeholder coordination through the YUS Conservation Area Management Committee (CAMC)
Scope of Work
The consultant will deliver an interlinked series of activities across 2026–2027, including:
Community‑Based Organisation (CBO) Capacity Strengthening
Conduct a literature review on CBOs in PNG protected areas
Develop an Organizational Capacity Assessment (OCA) template and interview guide
Train interviewers and support OCA implementation in YUS
Analyse OCA results and produce a comprehensive report
Develop training manuals covering:
Effective leadership
Public advocacy
Group facilitation
Conflict resolution
Persuasive presentation & public speaking
Project management
Deliver a Training‑of‑Trainers (ToT) program for CBO leaders
Develop coaching and guidance tools for ongoing mentoring
Strengthening Community Engagement in Ward & LLG Planning
Support Ward Councillors and Ward Development Committees in participatory planning
Facilitate community forums and governance workshops
Provide mentoring and monthly coaching transcripts
Support integration of community priorities into Ward, LLG, and District planning processes
Monitoring, Evaluation & Reporting
Develop Monitoring & Evaluation questionnaires and tools
Deliver M&E training and produce workshop reports
Produce a comprehensive end‑of‑project report
Deliverables & Compensation
Payments are tied agreed deliverables upon contracting. Additionally, TKCP will cover consultant travel, accommodation, workshop venues, and approved materials.
Required Qualifications
We are seeking organisations or individuals with:
Demonstrated experience in
community‑based conservation
,
protected area governance
, or
customary land management
in PNG
Strong background in
capacity building
,
training design
, and
facilitation
Experience working with
Ward Councils, LLGs, or community governance structures
Proven ability to produce high‑quality analytical reports and training materials
Excellent communication skills and cultural competency working with rural PNG communities
Ability to travel to remote areas and work collaboratively with TKCP staff

cover letter
outlining relevant experience
A
technical proposal
describing your approach to the Scope of Work
A
financial proposal
CVs of key personnel
Examples of previous similar work
IPA and IRC documents to confirm business entity.

8th May 2026

POSITION TITLE: EXECUTIVE PRINCIPAL, BALIMO COLLEGE
AREA:
Education
LOCATION:
Balimo College, New Town, Balimo, Delta Fly District, Western Province PNG
TYPE / DURATION:
Full time, 1 year contract, with contract extension possible
REPORTING TO:
Chair, Balimo College Governing Council
About Balimo College:
Balimo College’s vision is to advance Western Province by providing high-quality teaching, research and community engagement. The institute will foster pathways of teachers and health workers who are committed to improving access to vital services in Western Province. Balimo College will be a safe and supportive place for graduates and other professionals across the Western Province catchment region to return for life-long learning and ongoing professional development. The College will develop a community of education and health professionals committed to innovation, excellence and community advancement; by being the training College of choice for Papua New Guineans
Balimo College is an initiative of SDP implemented in partnership with KTF. SDP has a mandate to deliver development programs which provide lasting benefits to the people of Western Province. Our efforts are focused on Health, Education, Infrastructure and Agribusiness. We aim to supplement and complement the efforts of the Fly River Provincial Government (FRPG), in other words, help fill the gaps in the existing systems.
Balimo College is recognised as a Higher Education Institute by the National Higher Technical Education Board of the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology (DHERST). This recognition has been granted in accordance with the provisions of the Higher Education (General Provisions) Act 2014, as amended in 2020, under Section 14(1)(i) and 55(4)(a).
About the Role:
The Executive Principal is responsible for leading the strategic direction, operations, and administration of both the School of Teaching and the School of Nursing. Reporting to the Chair of the Governing Council, the GM will ensure that the College’s mission, vision, and goals are effectively upheld across all departments, ensuring high standards of education and community service. The GM will lead the executive team, including the Principals of both schools, and oversee all administrative, financial, and human resources functions.
The GM will have an in-depth knowledge of the ethos and purpose of the Balimo College and the principles by which it operates. The GM will have a firm understanding of the Western Province education and health contexts and the objectives of Balimo College to create pathways for rural communities into teaching and community health work.
Responsibilities:
Leadership & Strategy
Lead the strategic development and implementation of Balimo College’s vision, mission, and values.
Supervise and support the Principals of the School of Teaching and School of Nursing, ensuring alignment with institutional goals.
Foster collaboration between the schools to create a cohesive, innovative, and community-focused institution.
Establish and nurture a positive and inclusive college culture, promoting care, academic excellence, and integrity.
Drive initiatives to improve academic offerings, operational efficiency, and community engagement.
Operational Management
Ensure effective daily operations of Balimo College, including the coordination of academic programs, facilities, and student services.
Lead the College executive team to optimize the performance of both schools and streamline administrative processes.
Oversee the development and implementation of college policies, procedures, and systems in consultation with the two Principals, and in alignment with governing regulations and standards.
Coordinate the preparation of the academic calendar in collaboration with leadership teams.
Ensure compliance with PNG Department of Higher Education, Research, Science & Technology (DHERST) and other relevant authorities.
Human Resources and Capacity Building
Manage the recruitment, induction, and evaluation of staff in both schools in collaboration with the Principals and Governing Council.
Develop a performance management system and provide ongoing professional development opportunities for staff.
Foster leadership and career development among faculty and support staff.
Chair Staffing Committee meetings, overseeing decisions related to staffing structures, promotions, and performance.
Financial Oversight
Work with the Finance Manager and Finance, Audit & Risk Management Committee to develop and manage the College’s budget, ensuring financial sustainability.
Monitor and review financial performance, ensuring that spending aligns with the College’s strategic goals.
Act as a responsible signatory for financial decisions within the limits established by the Governing Council.
Academic Oversight
Ensure that the College’s educational programs meet high standards of quality and relevance to the community’s needs.
Oversee curriculum development and academic planning, in consultation with the two Principals, ensuring alignment with national and international standards.
Chair the Academic Board and receive reports from the Principals of the School of Teaching and School of Nursing in line with the Academic Board charter.
Foster partnerships with external stakeholders, including universities, government departments, and donors, to enhance the College’s programs and resources.
Community Engagement & Stakeholder Relations
Act as the primary spokesperson for Balimo College, building relationships with community leaders, government partners, and external partners.
Ensure active engagement with the local community to strengthen the College’s role as a hub for lifelong learning and professional development.
Promote and sustain a safe and inclusive environment for students, staff, and the broader community.
Risk Management & Compliance
Ensure adherence to all risk management, safety, and compliance requirements, particularly in workplace health and safety (WHS), child protection, Code of Conduct and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment.
Work with the Finance and Risk Management Committee to develop and implement a risk management framework.
Ensure that Balimo College operates in accordance with its safeguarding Policies, safeguarding the well-being of all students and staff.
Required Skills and Attributes:
Knowledge of:
A strong understanding of tertiary education and the specific challenges and opportunities in rural Papua New Guinea.
Experience in leadership roles within education, health or public sector institutions, preferably in PNG or similar contexts.
Proven financial management skills and experience managing budgets for educational institutions.
Familiarity with government policies and standards for tertiary education (DHERST, NDOE, PNG Nursing Council).
Leadership Abilities:
Demonstrated ability to lead, inspire, and manage teams across diverse functional areas.
Strong strategic thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to foster collaborative partnerships and manage stakeholder relationships effectively.
Formal Qualifications:
A Master’s degree in Education, Administration, or a related field.
Relevant professional experience in education leadership and management.
Personal Attributes:
A commitment to advancing education and health in rural PNG communities.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders.
High integrity, resilience, and the ability to lead by example. Applicants must have the right to work in PNG.
