26869.description:
BRING YOUR PASSION TO YOUR FUTURE WORKPLACE - JOIN OUR TEAM
DHL Express invites you to apply for the following opportunity open to
Port Moresby
residents only.
Residents of other centres need not apply.
Safety & Security Field Support Officer
We are seeking a capable Safety & Security Field Support Officer to ensure ongoing compliance with PNG Civil Aviation Regulations (CAR Part 109 and 100) and associated aviation security, cargo and mail security, cybersecurity, safety, and quality management requirements.
The role will provide on‑site governance and oversight for aviation security, safety, and OHS compliance, supports the management and closure audit findings, and reinforces a strong safety culture through effective risk management, hazard identification, incident reporting, and compliance with applicable PNG OHS legislation, DHL Group OHS standards, and recognised industry best practice.
Responsibilities will include:
Coordinate and perform routine internal safety and security audits, including regulatory audits and internal self‑assessments.
Monitor cargo handling practices to ensure secure storage of international cargo (including oversized consignments) and compliance with cargo screening and custody requirements.
Maintain and control the register of authorised screeners, including valid authorization letters and scope of screening authority.
Ensure background checks (police clearances) are completed, documented, and current for all staff performing security‑sensitive functions.
Support implementation and maintenance of the Safety Management System (SMS) and Quality Management System (QMS).
Promote a strong safety and security culture through awareness sessions, briefings, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Assist management in conducting workplace OHS audits country-wide in accordance with the approved audit timetable.
Assist with investigations of incidents, accidents, and near misses to identify root causes and corrective actions.
Ensure investigation outcomes and corrective actions are documented, tracked, and completed as required.
Act as the point of contact for WHS Committees across all sites, providing guidance and administrative support.
Provide WHS specialist advice, technical support, and coaching to Managers/ Supervisors, team members and WHS Committee members.
Assist with risk assessments for complex tasks and support frontline management and committees in conducting risk assessments for non‑complex activities.
Candidates' requirements for the role include:
Tertiary qualifications in Business Management, Aviation Management, Occupational Health & Safety or related discipline.
Knowledge of PNG Civil Aviation Regulations (CAR Part 109 and 100) and PNG OHS legislation.
Minimum 3–5 years’ experience in safety, security, compliance, or operational risk management.
Demonstrated experience supporting regulatory audits and closing audit findings (CASA or equivalent authority).
Practical experience in cargo and mail security, and safety oversight within an operational environment.
Strong communication skills and excellent problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated ability to manage self in a high energy environment.
Demonstrated ability to work well under pressure.
Valid Identification Card (NID/ Birth Certificate/ Passport/ Driver’s License).
Current class 6 driver’s license and current police clearance certificate.

26640.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our growing exploration team as our drilling program expands in 2026 and 2027, you will provide front line leadership, support, mentoring and service in all geology activities, associated with exploration and resource drilling, core processing, sample analysis and resource evaluation. Observe and adhere to the workplace health & safety policies to ensure safety of employee’s contractors and stakeholders.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Provide appropriate leadership, guidance mentoring and support in geology services to exploration.
Manage all Exploration sampling activities – including but not limited to drilling, rock chip, soil sampling.
Surveying and mapping designated areas / prospects.
Analysing geological data using specialist computer applications.
Preparing reports, both internal and statutory, physicals and forecast. Complete all reports in a timely manner, adhering to strict deadlines.
Ensure correct QA/QC protocols are adhered to.
Drill hole planning, designs and roll out.
Ensuring / authorising that geotechnical inspections of drill pads are completed, pre- and post-construction and pre-drilling. Ensure that regular monitoring of drill pads is carried out.
Coordinate drill pads design and construction in a timely manner.
Ensure logging of core by geologist is accurate, consistent, and complete; includes inspecting core logs and comparing with drill core.
Carry out weekly database checks to ensure logging is complete and following up where incomplete.
Maintain accuracy at all times of processing data collected by core shed technicians and data base assistants (core mark-up, recovery, RQD, magnetic susceptibility, ASD, XRF, core photography, cutting and sampling).
Ensure that Camp Managers send core photos, timesheets, and daily reports daily.
Establish a high-performance culture by motivating team members to achieve a high level of performance and by rewarding and recognising high performance.
Ensure effective processes are in place for communicating relevant information, including company, site, department, and team performance, to all team members.
Direct and train employees on the Exploration SOP.
Continuously mentor and coach geology technicians on effective sampling, core processing techniques.
Actively review the work performance of geology and technicians and provide feedback to the Vice President (Exploration and Deputy Exploration including the talent and succession planning for designated key roles.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Ensure exploration drilling and sampling is conducted by competent technicians in a safe manner and in accordance with established procedures.
About You
To be considered for this position, it is essential that applicants have the following
Bachelor`s Degree in Geology (Preferable), Geophysics or Geoscience
7+ years relevant mining or exploration work experience essential.
Computer proficiency in MS Office suite and the ability to analyse numerical and graphical data, including experience with 3D modelling software.
Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble-shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

26870.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
At Newmont, our people and safe performance are fundamental to our success. As Advisor, Advisor People, Training (Asset Management Fixed), you will be instrumental in building and sustaining workforce capability across Fixed Plant Maintenance, with a strong focus on electrical training and compliance.
Your work will ensure our people are competent, authorised, and trained in line with regulatory requirements and Newmont standards, directly supporting operational safety, reliability, and continuous improvement across site.
As part of our team, you will
In this role, you will:
Evaluate Fixed Plant training needs, with a strong focus on electrical compliance and competency assurance, and identify skill gaps.
Design, develop, and coordinate comprehensive training programs aligned to internal, statutory, and regulatory requirements.
Create engaging training materials and learning modules that support continuous improvement and adult learning principles.
Deliver and coordinate training sessions across Fixed Plant Maintenance teams.
Maintain and assure electrical competency frameworks, including authorisation, verification, refresher, and gap‑closure processes.
Ensure training programs align with site electrical safety rules, statutory obligations, and Newmont standards.
Partner with Electrical Engineering, HSE, site leadership, and external training providers to ensure training reflects current risk controls and best practice.
Incorporate learnings from audits, inspections, and incident investigations into training content and on‑the‑job training.
Maintain and manage electrical competencies, authorisations, and compliance records within the Learning Management System (LMS).
Develop, review, and continuously improve training materials, facilitator guides, verification of competency processes, On‑the‑Job Training (OJT), and online learning content.
Conduct field observations and engage with operational leaders to understand workforce capability needs and tailor training solutions.
Maintain audit‑ready training and competency records demonstrating compliance.
Support safety leadership by coaching teams, participating in investigations, and reinforcing safe work practices.
Promote proactive safety behaviours, coach employees, and contribute to incident investigations and continuous improvement initiatives.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You will bring:
Electrical trade certification (instrumentation desirable).
Formal qualifications in Training & Assessment, Education, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience in technical training, ideally within mining, processing plants, or the resources sector.
Strong understanding of electrical compliance frameworks, competency assurance, authorisation systems, and refresher training requirements.
Proven ability to design and deliver training aligned to regulatory and site standards.
Experience working with compliance, audit, and regulatory environments.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across a diverse workforce.
Strong computer literacy, including Microsoft Office and training management systems
Auditor certification and leadership experience (desirable)
Proven facilitation, coaching, and mentoring capability across diverse operational teams.
Strong technical writing skills with the ability to translate standards into effective training materials.
Proficiency in adult learning principles and vocational education (VET) frameworks
Strong computer literacy, including Microsoft Office.
The capability to work with autonomy and minimal supervision, effectively managing priorities when provided with clear direction and resources.
A solutions‑focused mindset.
A clear commitment to safety, continuous improvement, and Newmont’s values.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 day shift Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will operate in a dynamic operational environment, supporting compliance across Fixed Plant Maintenance without holding operational electrical authority, while providing assurance that all electrical training and competency requirements are met.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you’ll be part of a global organisation committed to safety, integrity, inclusion, and sustainability. We offer:
The opportunity to make a meaningful impact on workforce capability and safety.
A supportive and inclusive workplace where expertise is valued.
Exposure to world‑class mining operations and systems.
Ongoing development opportunities within a global organisation.
The chance to contribute to safe, responsible, and sustainable mining.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you! Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 42058 before the advertised closing date: 7 May 2026.
Apply

26897.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Technician Dogging/Rigging will perform rigging and dogman activities in support of Mobile Crane and Fixed Plant operations across process plant and mining environments, including crushing, grinding, flotation, conveyor systems, support facilities, and associated ancillary equipment, in accordance with approved site procedures, lift plans, and safety standards.
Essential Duties
Performs rigging and dogman activities in the field on fixed and mobile plant equipment, structures, and processing facility components.
Communicates effectively with Supervisors, Crane Operators, and other work groups regarding day-to-day technical issues by providing timely updates, seeking input where required, and supporting maintenance priorities while building effective working relationships across operations.
Escalates issues, delays, or constraints that may impact the safe or timely execution of assigned tasks.
Conducts preventative maintenance inspections on plant equipment and rigging gear as directed, in accordance with site procedures.
Ensures the rigging shed, tools, and equipment within the area of responsibility are maintained in a safe and serviceable condition.
Applies skills and experience to tasks and actively supports the development of others through knowledge sharing and on-the-job guidance.
Training & Experience
3–5 years of relevant work experience, preferably within heavy industry and ideally in a mining environment
Intermediate to advanced rigging and dogman competency (Essential).
Demonstrated experience performing rigging and dogman activities across fixed and mobile plant equipment and infrastructure.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Self-motivated, with the ability to work autonomously when required.
High attention to detail, supported by effective time management and task prioritisation skills.
Well-developed active listening and interpersonal skills, enabling effective collaboration across work groups.
Intermediate to advanced rigging and dogman competency (Essential).
Minimum Grade 10 education or equivalent (Essential).
PNG National Driver’s License (Essential).
Works in accordance with the PNG Mine Safety Act, Newmont Standards, safety policies and procedures, environmental policies, and all relevant departmental operating procedures.
Demonstrated sound knowledge of rigging and dogman activities, including experience supporting mobile crane operations.

This is a FIFO role on a 28/14 rotating day and night shift roster.

Fixed term contract up to 30 June 2028 (with possible 2 year extension)
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Open to PNG national candidates only
About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
The PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its TVET sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program supports improvements in national quality assurance systems, technical college standards, graduate employability, and Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG.
The program aligns with the broader goals of the Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029, which emphasizes locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth, as well as PNG’s Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020002E.
Purpose of Position
The Communications and Public Diplomacy Manager is responsible for the delivery of SWLT’s communications and public diplomacy activities, helping to showcase SWLT in an engaging way, to raise awareness of Australia’s support for PNG’s TVET sector, and to draw public attention to TVET education as a successful pathway to in demand careers.
Primary Responsibilities
The
Communications and Public Diplomacy Manager
will be required to manage the implementation of the Public Diplomacy Strategy and workplan, coordinate stakeholder engagement, and contribute to content development and reporting:
Work with the Public Diplomacy Specialist in the initial development of SWLT Communications and Public Diplomacy Strategy and associated Public Diplomacy workplan (DFAT deliverable), ensuring alignment to PNG-Australia Partnership key messages and branding
Actively contribute to on-going management, delivery and updating of strategy and workplan documents to keep them relevant, impactful and effective
Build collaborative relationships with team members, drawing on technical advice and individual experience and expertise.
Work with the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology (DHERST) public diplomacy unit and other key public diplomacy stakeholders to leverage and extend reach
Assist in developing locally relevant communications materials, including social media content, newsletters, and case studies, working with the SWLT MEL team to capture content for public diplomacy efforts
Support the planning, tracking and management of communications and public diplomacy budgets, including supplier costs and event expenditures with support from Operations and Finance
Lead communications and public diplomacy reporting, including tracking performance, contributing to MEL inputs, and preparing regular updates on workplan delivery and results.
Managing aspects of program photography and videography, including permissions, editing, storing and publishing
Seek to develop new and innovative ways of developing and delivering content with key messaging sought through direct student engagement
Utilise digital analytics and survey mythologies to measure impact of messaging
Manage the media relations and monitoring for SWLT, including developing a media contact list, creating media releases and op-eds, acting as Media Liaison as authorised, keeping track of media coverage and public engagement, and contributing to MEL reporting on reach and effectiveness
Coordinate logistics and planning for public diplomacy events, campaigns, and stakeholder engagements, including supporting terms of references for events and developing budgets
Collaborate with technical teams to ensure communications reflect SWLT principles and program objectives
Provide strategic advice and support in the recruitment of the Public Diplomacy Coordinator, and provide leadership and coaching to this role on an ongoing basis
Understand and contribute to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required
Adhere to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and commit to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately
Model, contribute to and support an office culture of learning and performance with colleagues, junior staff and counterparts
This role supports and upholds the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, such as reducing resource use and promoting climate-friendly practices
Contribute to the development and implementation of solutions that deliver value and ensure SWLT principles are embedded within program delivery.
Reporting Requirements
This role reports to the Deputy Director – Development Priorities and will have approximately one (1) direct report.
Reporting requirements may include but are not limited to:
Supporting inputs to the SWLT MEL Framework and Plan
Other project reporting as required.
Minimum Experience Required
The candidate needs to demonstrate proven experience in the following areas:
Delivering effective communications and marketing campaigns, with past experience in private sector or with donor funded programs
Strong writing, editing and storytelling skills
Ability to use of a range of communications and public diplomacy modalities and the hardware and software needed in their creation including:
- Social media platforms and content
- Videography
- Photography
- Visual graphics – charts, animations, infographics
- Newspaper and TV news ready content
Events planning and coordination
An understanding of the political and cultural context in PNG with the ability to work respectfully with partner government counterparts
Proven ability to work with MEL frameworks or communication monitoring tools
Experience coaching and mentoring junior colleagues and providing positive and constructive support that enables them to learn and grow
Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team
Experience and/or knowledge of the TVET or higher education sector in PNG would be advantageous
Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion.
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.
To Apply
Please submit your application online, including your CV and brief cover letter, outlining your suitability in line with the requirements of the position via

26734.description:
Communications and Advocacy Manager
Position Description
Reporting to:
Director, Program Development and Quality (PDQ)
--       Dotted reporting line to Pacific Advocacy Advisor and Pacific Communications Manager
Work location:
Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Department:
PDQ
Budget holder:
No
Team:
PDQ Team
Direct reports:
No permanent direct reports. Management of freelancers may be required.
Role Purpose and Scope
The Advocacy and Communications (A&C) Manager will take lead in designing and delivering innovative communications and advocacy strategies that inspire public support and actions, influence policy decisions and drive the agenda for children in Papua New Guinea. She/He is expected to organise and deliver advocacy initiatives aimed at changing practices for betterment of children’s lives at community and national levels, including advocacy workshops and mentoring young activists and groups. Working with the Program Development and Quality Director (DPDQ), they will lead on implementing the Save the Children’s Pacific Advocacy Strategy in PNG.
The A&C Manager is responsible for managing the PNG Country Office’s media-related activities as well as its social media and online platforms to ensure published information is up to date, of a high quality, accurate and in line with organizational policies and procedures. She/He will also support the capacity building of Save the Children PNG staff in identifying and undertaking communications to achieve brand consistency in line with organizational branding policy standards and donor requirements.
Dimensions:
The A&C Manager has both an internal and external orientation but works closely with the DPDQ, the Pacific Communications Manager and program implementation teams internally in facilitating the planning, implementation and monitoring of advocacy, media and communication initiatives. Externally, the role will be expected to strategically position Save the children in PNG as a leading provider of life changing interventions for children and their families around the Country.
Working contacts
Internal: PDQ team members, program managers and various implementation team members, thematic leads, consultants, visitors, communication and advocacy teams from the regional office and member countries.
External: Media, child rights groups, other civil society organisations, service providers, local authorities, and consortium members, partners, international and domestic publics.
Key Areas of Accountability
Advocacy
With the PDQ Director, lead the development and coordination of Save the Children PNG’s Advocacy Strategy under the guidance and support from Save the Children Australia Policy Team.
Support the programme teams in implementing advocacy activities taking advantage of key moments to deliver on the Country Office advocacy objectives.
Work closely with thematic advisors involved in advocacy campaigns, public mobilization and engagements to create moments and opportunities for advocacy and change.
Build and maintain effective, collaborative relationships with Save the Children’s Australia Policy Unit, other Pacific Country Offices, to ensure common messages and effective advocacy efforts.
Build and maintain effective relationships with government stakeholders, civil society representatives, UN, INGOs, and Academia to advance Save the Children’s advocacy efforts.
Support Save the Children PNG’s engagement in regional and global advocacy efforts through contribution of stories, videos, photos etc. to highlight Country Office achievements within such initiatives.
Advocacy campaigns
Support the co-creation of advocacy campaigns at national and global levels with children and youth activists, including Save the Children Project Managers to explore opportunities for Children’s voices to be heard in project designs.
Work closely with thematic advisors involved in advocacy, public mobilization and engagements to create moments and opportunities for campaigning.
Build and maintain effective, collaborative relationships with Save the Children’s Australia, Pacific Country Offices, Pacific regional and global advocacy teams ensuring consistent approaches, common messages and effective campaign events.
External
Communications
Develop a communication strategy, guidelines and plan for the Country Office.
Lead the development and dissemination of relevant real-time humanitarian and development situational reports/materials.
Lead the dissemination of Save the Children brand to make it recognised, respected, accepted, and protected at all levels.
Support project leads and technical specialists to identify and document stories of change and case studies, success stories that communicate the impact of our work and for use in media work and for quality reporting purposes.
Take lead in reviewing and presenting stories, photos, messaging, fact sheets and multimedia products for Save the Children’s key public audience.
Support the field program teams in ensuring Save the Children brand and donor requirements are fulfilled for visibility and communications materials.
Work closely with the program teams on graphic design and production of materials for fundraising and advocacy campaigns.
Produce other external targeted products on an ad hoc basis as necessary and requested by the supervisor.
Train key senior staff on communications and media and support the Country Director and Senior Management teams in their roles as the Save the Children PNG designated spokespersons.
Media
Develop media strategy/guidelines to guide the engagement of Save the Children in PNG office with media.
Develop, and implement a social media strategy that communicates the impact of our work and speaks to the Papua New Guinea and Pacific public, including regularly updating the platforms.
Ensure that all media messages and engagements are approved by the line manager and Country Director.
Identify media issues, prepare media messages, assess appropriate media for communicating those messages and facilitate the process of disseminating/communicating those messages.
Take lead in media relations and, as appropriate, establish proactive and beneficial relationship with media houses that can help in advancing children’s rights at policy and program levels as well as identify opportunities to profile Save the Children work.
Ensure that any action undertaken to implement communications or media work in country is compliant with Save the Children’s communications and branding standards and has been duly approved by the Country Director.
Familiarise self with the work of Save the Children in Papua New Guinea to effectively represent the organisation in media engagements where relevant.
Draft media briefings, talking points, Q&As, press releases and media statements based on advocacy priorities identified by thematic technical advisors.
Internal Communication
Compile and develop Save the Children’s Country reports, sit reps and newsletters with thematic advisors and project managers as required.
Provide assistance to content and layout of creative promotional materials such as leaflets, fact sheets, info graphics, creative audiovisual information, brochures and other communications materials.
Lead the development of a communications calendar capturing priorities of actions and products for the Country Office.
Management of internal communications content including archiving, uploading on content hub, website and other platforms.
MEAL PDQ
With support from Save the Children Australia, develop and put in place systems to monitor and measure the impact of the PNG advocacy and communications strategies, as well as systematically sharing these achievements in the most appropriate way with the SMT.
Share success stories and learning related to Advocacy and Communications initiatives spearheaded in PNG with the Pacific Team, Melbourne Office, Pacific regional and global working groups and/or communities of practice.
Contribute to proposal development processes where advocacy and communication activities are present.
Health, Safety, Security and Risk Management
Be a role model for safety and security, including complying with all safety instructions and training given at the workplace.
Act in a safe manner at all times, including complying with all safety instructions and training given at the workplace.
Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.
Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.
Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with your team’s everyday work and ensure appropriate mitigation measures are applied.
Ensure staff have completed all required training and have up-to-date background and working with children checks.
Lead and promote a culture of strong governance promoting employee health, safety and security and operational risk management.
Ensure safety and security of staff and equipment during implementation of advocacy and communication activities.
Child protection and safeguarding requirements
Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times.
Comply with the Child Safeguarding Code of Conduct and child safeguarding and protection policies and standards (click
here
to view further details).
Demonstrate the highest standards of behaviour towards children in both your private and professional life.
Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being a part of the Save the Children family.
Always maintain a safe and positive relationship when working with children and young people.
Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.
Ensure staff have completed background checks and are trained in child safeguarding in line with organisational and program requirements.
Person Specification
Essential knowledge or experience
Ability to multitask, work under pressure and to meet tigh

Supervisor – Underground Electrical
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea (PNG). As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mobile Maintenance Department as a
Supervisor – Underground Electrical.
About the role
Reporting to the Forman - Underground Maintenance, the Supervisor - Underground Electrical will oversee the electrical maintenance and installation activities within New Porgera Limited’s (NPL) underground operations. This role ensures that all electrical systems and equipment are maintained, repaired, and installed to the highest standards, supporting safe and efficient mining operations. The Supervisor will lead a team of electricians, ensuring compliance with all safety standards and operational objectives while providing technical expertise and leadership.
In this role, you will
:
Supervise and lead a team of electricians and trade assistants providing guidance, support and technical expertise.
Carry out maintenance, fault finding, and repair of underground electrical infrastructure and associated mining assets
Install, inspect and verify electrical installations in accordance with electrical codes and New Porgera Limited requirements
Respond promptly to electrical breakdowns, diagnose faults, and implement effective solutions to minimize downtime.
Plan, coordinate and execute maintenance activities using efficient servicing strategies to achieve service time targets and schedule compliance
Accurately document maintenance work, including tasks completed, materials used, and identified issues
Collaborate with the maintenance and operations teams to ensure electrical systems meet operational demands.
Assist in maintaining an inventory of spare parts and tools necessary for electrical maintenance tasks.
Adhere to strict health and safety standards while working in challenging underground environments.
Uphold high standards of health and safety awareness, ensuring compliance with NPL’s Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all safety procedures.
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
A Trade Certificate in Electrical.
Manual driving license
Minimum of 5 years’ experience in electrical maintenance in the Mining, Oil and Gas or Heavy industry environment, including demonstrated experience in a supervisory role.
Strong knowledge of underground electrical systems, including high-voltage and low-voltage equipment.
Proven ability to lead and manage a team effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.
Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills for complex electrical systems.
Sound knowledge and demonstrated understanding of AS/NZS electrical standards
Solid understanding of workplace health and safety regulations, particularly in underground mining.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate across teams.
Proficient in using maintenance management systems and Microsoft Office applications.
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a as Supervisor – Underground Electrical. (NS)
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a as Supervisor – Underground Electrical. This role offers a unique opportunity to lead a dynamic team, work with cutting-edge underground mining technology, and contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your leadership and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.
Note
: This advert will be open until
10
th
of May,2026
.  If you do not hear from NPL within two (2) weeks of this date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity
.
Apply

Mechanical Workshop Storeman (3 Positions)
Join a Market Leader in PNG Technology & Infrastructure
MasterSystems Technologies
is expanding. We are currently seeking
three (3) dedicated Mechanical Workshop Storemen
to join our operations—one for each of our key branches:
Lae
Port Moresby
Mount Hagen
At MasterSystems, we deliver the best service in PNG. To do that, we need a backbone of precision in our workshops. You will be responsible for ensuring our mechanics have the right parts at the right time to keep our clients moving.
The Role
You will take full ownership of your branch’s workshop stores, managing everything from high-turnover consumables to specialized automotive parts. We are looking for individuals who take pride in 100% inventory accuracy and a highly organized workspace.

Workshop Support:

Minimum Grade 12 completion.
Experience:

Good knowledge of automotive/mechanical parts and strong computer literacy.

Background:
SCHEDULE 1
Duties and Responsibilities of Position
The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skillsets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:
http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org
Position Description
The Senior Program Officer (SPO), Malaria is CHAI PNG’s national-level malaria implementation lead, responsible for driving CHAI’s malaria control activities and ensuring coordinated delivery across provincial implementation.
Reporting to the Program Lead, the SPO will focus on implementation excellence across CHAI’s three malaria technical pillars case management, supply chain, and surveillance while working in close partnership with the National Malaria Control Program (NMCP) at NDoH.
The SPO will provide technical oversight and coordination support to the Program Officer, Malaria in Madang Province, maintaining weekly communication to ensure that provincial activities remain aligned with national priorities.
This is an implementation-focused role requiring strong technical knowledge of malaria programming, the ability to maintain consistent progress independently while the Program Lead attends to other program areas, and proven field experience.
The SPO must demonstrate strong problem-solving skills, a practical and detail-oriented approach, a solid track record of project implementation, and a clear understanding of the National Malaria Program.

26771.description:
Workshop Technician — Electronic Equipment
Keynote Limited  --  Port Moresby  --  Full-time, permanent
Do you have a passion for audio and electronics? Keynote Limited — PNG's leading musical instrument and professional audio retailer — is looking for a skilled Workshop Technician to join our Port Moresby service team.
About the role
Working from our Port Moresby workshop, you'll diagnose and repair a wide range of professional audio equipment (mixers, amplifiers, PA systems) and electronic musical instruments (keyboards, digital pianos, guitar amps). This is a bench-based role for someone who enjoys problem-solving, takes pride in quality workmanship, and wants to be part of a team that keeps the music playing across Papua New Guinea.
What you'll be doing
Fault-finding and repairing professional audio and electronic music equipment to component level
Performing preventive maintenance and routine servicing
Providing accurate repair estimates and clear job documentation
Managing your own repair queue and meeting turnaround commitments
Supporting the sales team with technical product knowledge
What we're looking for
2–5 years of hands-on bench repair experience in pro audio or electronic musical instruments
Certificate or diploma in electronics or electrical engineering (or equivalent trade experience)
Solid skills with diagnostic tools — multimeters, oscilloscopes, signal generators
Competent soldering skills to component level
Methodical, thorough, and able to juggle multiple jobs at once
PNG citizen or resident with the right to work in Papua New Guinea
Why Keynote?
PNG's largest and most established music and audio business, operating since 1968
Work with leading international brands including Yamaha, QSC, Mackie, Roland, and more
A stable, full-time role with a competitive salary package (negotiable based on experience)
Nasfund superannuation contributions as required by law
Supportive team environment where technical expertise is genuinely valued

26774.description:
About Newmont
Newmont is the world’s leading gold company, producing gold as well as copper, silver, zinc, lead and molybdenum across operations in Australia, Papua New Guinea, Africa, Latin America and North America.
In Australia, Newmont operates across Western Australia, the Northern Territory and New South Wales, supported by teams in Perth, Brisbane and Melbourne.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
Reporting to the Site Supply Chain Lead at Lihir, the Advisor, Contract Management supports the effective delivery and performance of site‑based contracts, ensuring alignment with procurement strategies, governance frameworks, and operational requirements, and contributes to the overall success and continuity of site operations.
The role coordinates and oversees post‑award contract management activities across the contract lifecycle, maintains effective supplier relationships, supports cost optimisation initiatives, and ensures site contracts deliver agreed safety, operational, and commercial outcomes. The role also supports local content, community engagement, and sustainability objectives through monitoring supplier compliance with contractual requirements.
As part of our team you will
Manage post‑award site contracts across their lifecycle, ensuring supplier performance, compliance, and strategic alignment.
Support contract performance reviews and reporting to drive improvement and value.
Maintain effective relationships with internal stakeholders and suppliers.
Assist with contract variations, negotiations, and dispute management.
Conduct contract audits and compliance reviews and track follow‑up actions.
Identify and support cost reduction and savings opportunities.
Contribute to ad hoc and continuous improvement initiatives.
Prerequisites for your success in the role
Strong attention to detail with solid contract administration capability
Experience in contract management, procurement, or supply chain roles
Exposure to ERP and supply chain systems (e.g. SAP, Ariba)
Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
Ability to manage multiple priorities across contracts and projects
Experience in operational industries (e.g. Mining, Oil & Gas, Construction, Supply Chain or Logistics)
Tertiary qualification or equivalent experience in Business, Commerce, Supply Chain, Law, or related discipline.
Your work environment
This role is based at Lihir, with preference for Local Lihirians and PNG Nationals, however FIFO arrangements may be considered for the right candidate.
Working on site requires adaptability, commitment to roster schedules, and a strong safety mindset in a dynamic operational environment.
At Newmont, people create the value in the metals we mine responsibly and are ambassadors in the communities where they live and work. As a team, we foster an environment in support of our people vision, where everyone belongs, thrives and is valued. We have built a diverse and inclusive workplace where our people can bring their differences to support delivering results together.
Join us and unearth your potential in a global company that is at the forefront of shaping the future of the mining industry.
Applications close Sunday 3 May, 2026
Apply

26510.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will be responsible for ensuring the safe and efficient delivery of drilling pads to support the Company’s exploration drilling programs. Work will be undertaken in remote, mountainous, and steep terrain, and must be carried out in strict accordance with K92 Mining site requirements, standards, and procedures.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operate and maintain mini excavators and skid steer loaders in accordance with K92 Plant Operations & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems.
Conduct pre-start inspections and basic troubleshooting on equipment to identify and address potential issues.
Construct drill pads, helipads, and access walkways in a mountainous exploration environment.
Monitor the condition of work pads and surrounding areas, ensuring ongoing safety and stability.
Collaborate with Geotechnical and Drilling Supervisors to plan and optimise drill pad locations, sumps, and drainage systems.
Respond to routine and emergency maintenance or support requests across the exploration site to minimise equipment downtime.
Support the Exploration Supervisor in identifying and rectifying defects in equipment and work areas to optimise availability, reliability, and overall performance.
Work closely with the Exploration Supervisor to monitor equipment performance and identify improvement opportunities.
Contribute to initiatives that maximise operational results, reduce risk, and support cost management objectives.
Actively promote a safe and healthy workplace culture.
Demonstrate personal accountability for health and safety, while reinforcing legal obligations, safe work practices, and HSE standards across the team.
Maintain high standards of housekeeping within and around designated work areas.
Ensure equipment maintenance is carried out by competent personnel in a safe manner and in accordance with established procedures.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must obtain a minimum qualification of Grade 10 or above with experience in operating with a Class 4 License that allows operation of an Excavator on public roads and must have 2+ years’ experience in operating different types of equipment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Must have knowledge of small excavator performance capabilities
Previous experience as an excavator operator smaller than 20 T
Knowledge of exploration drilling activities
Must have commitment to safety
Must have ability to work autonomously independent with limited supervision
Must demonstrate abilities to work within a team environment
Previous experience working within the mining industry
General knowledge of mobile equipment
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.

Position Title: Lecturer - School of Law                                                                                                    Department: School of Law
Reports To: Head of School / Pro-Vice Chancellor (Academic)
Institution: IBSUniversity, 11Mile Campus
Partner Institution: Southern Cross University
Location: Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Employment Type: Full-Time
ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades &  Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999 and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face-to-face in Papua New Guinea
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016, for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, CISCO, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
Established partnerships with Oracle Academy, Red Hat Academy, and the All-India Management Association (AIMA), among others.
To bridge the gap between academia and industry, facilitated Memoranda of Understanding with organisations such as BSP, Telikom, CPL, Vodafone, Women’s Micro Bank, Theodist, Barlow Industries, and CEFI.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching, learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and partners.
Position Overview
The Lecturer of School of Law is responsible for delivering high-quality teaching, learning, and academic support in Law courses offered at IBSUniversity in collaboration with Southern Cross University. The role ensures that teaching aligns with international academic standards while contextualizing learning to Papua New Guinea’s legal environment.
The lecturer contributes to student success through innovative teaching practices, research, and industry engagement consistent with the Southern Cross Modules, which emphasizes focused, applied, and student-centred learning.
Key Responsibilities
Teaching & Learning
Deliver undergraduate (and/or postgraduate) law units in accordance with SCU-approved curriculum.
Facilitate lectures, tutorials, workshops, and online learning sessions.
Apply student-centred and interactive teaching methodologies aligned with the SCU teaching model.
Develop lesson plans, teaching materials, and case-based learning activities.
Support blended learning (face-to-face and digital platforms).
Assessment & Academic Administration
Design, administer, and grade assessments in line with SCU academic standards.
Provide timely and constructive feedback to students.
Maintain accurate academic records and reporting.
Ensure compliance with academic integrity and quality assurance policies.
Student Support
Provide academic advising and mentoring to students.
Identify and support students at risk.
Facilitate consultation sessions and academic support workshops.
Research & Scholarly Activity
Engage in legal research relevant to Papua New Guinea and the broader region.
Contribute to publications, conferences, and academic forums.
Support IBSU’s research initiatives and journal contributions.
Industry & Community Engagement
Maintain connections with legal practitioners, courts, and regulatory bodies.
Incorporate practical legal perspectives into teaching.
Participate in community outreach and legal awareness initiatives.
Quality Assurance & Compliance
Ensure delivery meets both IBSU and SCU academic standards.
Participate in moderation, curriculum review, and accreditation processes.
Adhere to university policies, procedures, and ethical standards.
Qualifications & Experience
Essential
Master’s Degree in Law (LLM) or related field (PhD preferred)
Bachelor of Laws (LLB) from a recognized institution
Teaching experience in higher education
Strong knowledge of legal systems (PNG and/or common law systems)
Desirable
Admission to legal practice (PNG or other jurisdiction)
Experience with international or transnational education programs
Research publications in law or related fields
Experience with blended or online learning platforms
Skills & Competencies
Strong teaching and presentation skills
Curriculum development and assessment design
Research and analytical skills
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Ability to adapt to international academic frameworks
Cultural awareness and contextual understanding of PNG
Working Relationships
Internal: Faculty members, academic administration, student services
External: Southern Cross University academic teams, legal professionals, regulatory bodies
Work Environment
Academic setting with blended teaching (classroom + online)
Structured teaching terms aligned with SCU model (short, intensive delivery cycles)

26849.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
You’ll play a critical role in keeping Newmont’s mining fleet safe, reliable, and production‑ready by delivering high‑quality fabrication and welding solutions that directly support mining operations at Lihir. Your workmanship will help minimise downtime and ensure equipment performs to standard in a demanding operating environment.
As part of our team, you will
Perform fabrication, welding, repair, and modification work on heavy mining equipment
Execute cutting, gouging, shaping, and welding tasks to OEM and Newmont standards
Support planned maintenance and respond to breakdowns as required
Troubleshoot equipment issues and assist with effective repair solutions
Use Newmont’s SAP database for work order generation, time entry, and job completion
Maintain tools and equipment in a safe and serviceable condition
Work safely in confined spaces and at heights when required
Actively contribute to safety performance and continuous improvement
Share knowledge and support the development of apprentices and team members
Prerequisites for your success in this role
PNG Level 3 Trade Qualification in Metal Fabrication & Welding
Welding qualification to ISO 9606‑1 or willingness to obtain
Minimum 5 years post‑apprenticeship experience
Proven experience welding and fabricating heavy mining equipment
Strong capability using MMAW, MIG, and FCAW in vertical and overhead positions
Experience with carbon arc gouging, thermic lancing, and oxy‑fuel cutting
Ability to read plans, take accurate measurements, and deliver quality workmanship
Strong safety mindset and ability to follow procedures
Self‑motivated, reliable, and able to work effectively in a team
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 28:14 Day / Night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

26844.description:
Welfare Officer
Hargy Oil Palms Limited (HOPL) is an Oil Palm plantation company based in Bialla, West New Britain Province. A remote location is situated approximately 2 and half hours’ drive east of Kimbe town.
HOPL currently has a vacancy for a suitably qualified and experienced Welfare Officer who will join its Human Resources Department and deliver support services to HOPL Employees and immediate family.
Primary Objectives:
This role is critical in promoting employee wellbeing, supporting welfare-related matters, and strengthening positive workplace relationships.
Competencies
To perform the job successfully, it is expected that the applicant must demonstrate the following competencies:
Provide welfare support and counselling to employees and their families
Address workplace and personal welfare concerns in a confidential and professional manner
Coordinate employee wellbeing programs
Liaise with management, medical services and other key stakeholders
Conduct welfare investigations and maintain accurate case records
Support compliance with company policies, labour laws, and social standards
Contribute to a safe, respectful, and supportive working environment
Education and Background
Diploma or Degree in Counselling or similar.
Previous experience in welfare or counselling role.
Strong communication, counselling, and interpersonal skills
High level of confidentiality, integrity, and professionalism
Ability to work independently and handle sensitive cases
Willingness to work in a rural environment
Benefit
A competitive salary packages, including housing, utilities and other benefits will be offered for the role and will be discussed during the interview.
Opportunity to work in a diverse and community-focused environment
A role where you can make a meaningful difference to employee wellbeing
If you believe that you have the necessary skills and experience, then please send your expression of interest with your CV to:
[email protected]
